ks-johnson-2026-commission-chair-crnkovi.name: Karen Crnkovich
ks-johnson-2026-commission-chair-crnkovi.bio: Owner of a Kansas City-area heating, cooling, ventilation and plumbing company and founder of the nonprofit Strong Homes, Strong Families.

positions.stance: Pledges to fight for real tax relief, to "cut property taxes, rein in runaway spending, and restore fiscal sanity to the county budget."
Will seek to eliminate waste, reduce non-essential spending and restore budget transparency; pledges "to lower taxes—not raise them."
Supports prioritizing pathways to single-family homeownership over more high-density development, and preventing institutional buyers from pricing out local families.

ks-johnson-2026-commission-chair-kelly-m.name: Mike Kelly
ks-johnson-2026-commission-chair-kelly-m.bio: Chair of the Johnson County Board of Commissioners, former Mayor of Roeland Park, and Senior Counsel at Husch Blackwell.

positions.stance: Aims to strengthen public safety partnerships and expand mental health and aging services.
Aims to complete major highway projects and ensure infrastructure keeps pace with both rural and urban development.
Aims to attract high-impact employers, expand support for small businesses, and invest in workforce development.
Pledges to continue responsible budgeting and invest in amenities such as parks and libraries that enhance daily life.

tx-collin-2026-county-judge-hill-chris.name: Chris Hill
tx-collin-2026-county-judge-hill-chris.bio: Collin County Judge and former county commissioner; previously an executive pastor and corporate controller.

positions.stance: Declared that "Every Texan is essential"; the site states "No lockdowns. No business closures. No mask mandates. No vaccine mandates."
Believes in planning ahead and investing in water, roads and mental-health infrastructure "before problems become crises" as the county grows.
Says responsible fiscal management means building a budget, setting priorities, and ensuring taxpayers get value for every dollar.
Supports giving those responsible for public safety the staffing, equipment, facilities and resources they need "before shortages become emergencies."
Opposes the $2.3 million spent replacing the county's voting system with a paper-ballot system, calling it a political stunt.
Says "Justice Shouldn't Depend on Who You Know" and the County Judge should focus on making sure justice moves forward.

tx-collin-2026-coa5-p3-kolodoski-matthew.name: Matthew Kolodoski
tx-collin-2026-coa5-p3-kolodoski-matthew.bio: Trial and appellate attorney and partner at a litigation firm; former law clerk to a U.S. District Court judge.

positions.stance: Says everyone is "entitled to equal and impartial justice" and a judge's duty is "to apply the law as written" without "favor, prejudice, or preconception."
Would be guided by "the rule of law, respect for the limited role of the judiciary," and fair, equal treatment of everyone before the court.

tx-collin-2026-coa5-p3-reichek-amanda.name: Amanda Reichek
tx-collin-2026-coa5-p3-reichek-amanda.bio: Former Justice, Place 10, on the Fifth District Court of Appeals (2019-2024), now at a Dallas litigation firm.

tx-collin-2026-coa5-p6-smith-ben.name: Ben Smith
tx-collin-2026-coa5-p6-smith-ben.bio: Judge of the 380th Judicial District Court in Collin County.

tx-collin-2026-coa5-p6-purdy-monica.name: Monica Purdy
tx-collin-2026-coa5-p6-purdy-monica.bio: Dallas County judge who previously served as a Municipal Court Judge and Associate Judge of the Civil District Courts.

tx-collin-2026-coa5-p8-wysocki-ashley.name: Ashley Wysocki
tx-collin-2026-coa5-p8-wysocki-ashley.bio: Presiding Judge of the 301st Judicial District Court of Dallas County; previously presiding judge of the 254th District Court.

tx-collin-2026-coa5-p8-plumlee-andrea.name: Andrea D. Plumlee
tx-collin-2026-coa5-p8-plumlee-andrea.bio: Judge of the 330th District Court in Dallas County for 15 years.

tx-collin-2026-dist-219-edgeworth-jennif.name: Jennifer Edgeworth
tx-collin-2026-dist-219-edgeworth-jennif.bio: Judge of the 219th Judicial District Court in Collin County; previously a civil litigation attorney for nineteen years.

positions.stance: Believes judges should be "fair, unbiased, and consistent."
Believes in the rule of law and "adhering to the language of the U.S Constitution and the Texas Constitution."
Believes judges "must be fiscally responsible and efficiently move cases through their courtrooms" because their work affects costs to Collin County taxpayers.

tx-collin-2026-dist-366-nowak-tom.name: Tom Nowak
tx-collin-2026-dist-366-nowak-tom.bio: Judge of the 366th District Court of Collin County since 2019.

tx-collin-2026-dist-494-pruitt-kathryn.name: Kathryn Pruitt
tx-collin-2026-dist-494-pruitt-kathryn.bio: Judge of the 494th District Court with over 31 years of legal experience in civil litigation and family law.

positions.stance: Says every case involves real people; approaches each decision "with seriousness and care, committed to weighing the facts carefully and applying the law faithfully."

tx-collin-2026-ccl-5-johnson-randy.name: Randy Johnson
tx-collin-2026-ccl-5-johnson-randy.bio: Judge of Collin County Court at Law No. 5; previously litigated civil and criminal cases for 38 years and served as a Dallas County assistant district attorney.

tx-collin-2026-ccl-6-bender-jay.name: Jay A. Bender
tx-collin-2026-ccl-6-bender-jay.bio: Judge of Collin County Court at Law No. 6 since 2010; former criminal defense attorney and assistant district attorney.

tx-denton-2026-county-judge-eads-andy.name: Andy Eads
tx-denton-2026-county-judge-eads-andy.bio: Denton County Judge and former County Commissioner of Precinct 4.

positions.stance: Will "continue to work to maintain a low tax rate while providing high quality county services."
Prioritizes improving transportation and road safety across the county to reduce commute times.
Supports providing law enforcement "the financial resources necessary" to do their job.
Works to attract employers by meeting with companies and "clearing paths for their business expansions."

tx-denton-2026-county-judge-pappas-nick.name: Nick Pappas
tx-denton-2026-county-judge-pappas-nick.bio: Retired, disabled Marine Corps veteran of multiple combat deployments.

positions.stance: Proposes weekend Commissioners Court sessions with public comment, livestreamed meetings, and posting the county budget and every county contract publicly.
Would publish the daily cost of holding one person in the county jail and what is being done to bring it down.
Wants infrastructure projects finished on time and on budget, and a published, uniform formula for county funding of roads inside cities.
Proposes "Three free meals a day for every kid" using federal grant dollars, and county-supported donation of surplus business food.
Supports around-the-clock shelter capacity run with nonprofit partners and using every eligible federal housing dollar on time.

tx-denton-2026-coa2-p2-taylor-chris.name: Chris Taylor
tx-denton-2026-coa2-p2-taylor-chris.bio: Presiding Judge of the 48th District Court in Tarrant County since 2021; formerly in the Tarrant County District Attorney's Civil Division.

tx-denton-2026-coa2-p7-walker-brian.name: Brian Walker
tx-denton-2026-coa2-p7-walker-brian.bio: Justice on the Second Court of Appeals; served nine years as a Judge Advocate in the U.S. Air Force Reserves.
